newsitem.title: USA: U.S. September budget surplus $35.37 bln.
newsitem.headline: U.S. September budget surplus $35.37 bln.

text.p: The government posted a budget surplus of $35.37 billion in September, the Treasury Department said Monday, five times the $7.19 billion surplus posted a year earlier in September 1995.
As previously announced by the White House, the total fiscal 1996 budget deficit for the year ended Sept 30 fell to $107.33 billion from $163.92 billion in fiscal 1995.
The last time the full-year deficit was lower was in 1981, when it totaled $79 billion.
In August this year, the budget was in deficit by $41.83 billion.
With presidential elections set for next week, the White House noted the overall budget deficit had fallen by 63 percent during the four years of the Clinton administration.
During September, total spending fell to $122.3 billion from $141.83 billion in August, while income climbed to $157.67 billion in September from $100 billion in August.
Total spending for all of fiscal 1996 was $1.56 trillion, up from $1.52 trillion in fiscal 1995.
Total government receipts, mainly from taxes, increased during fiscal 1996 to $1.45 trillion from $1.35 trillion in fiscal 1995.
The White House said that the deficit for fiscal 1996 represented 1.4 percent of gross domestic product, the lowest share since 1974.

Strong economic growth boosted tax receipts from individuals to $656.42 billion in fiscal 1996 from $590.24 billion in fiscal 1995. Corporate income taxes were up to $171.82 billion from $157 billion in fiscal 1995.
